newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Dollar/ringgit swaps steady despite curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/ringgit swaps steady despite curbs.

text.p: Dollar/ringgit swaps were unchanged early on Monday as local banks digested Bank Negara's announcement on Sunday of curbs on swaps, dealers said.
They said the market was extremely quiet as bank dealers waited for direction from their managements.
"We are still waiting for the official directive from Bank Negara. We have not heard anything from our management yet," said a dealer with one of Malaysia's largest banks.
He said the market was waiting to find out how the restrictions would work.
On Sunday, Bank Negara Malaysia said that from Monday, local banks will have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer.
The curbs are part of an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit which has been under attack from currency speculators over the past month.

"Banks are required with effect from 4 August 1997 to observe a limit of $2.0 million on outstanding non-commercial related ringgit offer side swap transactions with each foreign customer on a group basis," Bank Negara said in a statement.

It said banks which have exceeded the limit will not be allowed further swap transactions until the outstandings were reduced. A swap is a forward rate agreement for exchanging one currency for another, in this case ringgit for dollar.
Dealers said it was yet unclear how the swaps positions with individual overseas clients would be monitored.
"It is like what do we do if George Soros or somebody else does deals with us through 20 different sources or institutions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.

The Bank Negara statement said the move was to help control interest rates more effectively. The central bank has in the last two weeks been trying to lower interest rates in an effort to boost domestic economic activity.
Dealers said the curbs would bring down domestic swaps and push up overseas rates, effectively creating a two-tier market.
At 0115 GMT, one-month forward was at 45/75 points, three-month at 170/200 and six-month at 285/325.
But, the ringgit came down over 300 points to around 2.6050 to a dollar.
